messages:
maria: Heads-up: Partner asked for a concise perf/W report to go with the marketplace listing. They want a single recommended SKU + backup config. Need agreement on measurement protocol (how we sample watts, what steady state means).

tyler: I recommend using external PDU readings (rational: less vendor firmware variance) and syncing samples at 250ms. Steady-state = 90s window after warmup. We'll do seq=256 baseline and also a seq=1024 long-context check.

ajay: +1 on PDU. For SD comparisons we should normalize to tokens/sec and tokens/sec/W. Batches: 4, 16, 64, 256. Also record kernel thread counts and CUDA visible devices. Include quant modes: fp16, q4_0, q8_0.

maria: Good. What's our acceptance criteria for the listing? I want a simple rule so marketplace copy is deterministic.

tyler: Maybe: if best-config tokens/sec/W >= 90% of our internal certified baseline, list as "Recommended". If between 70-90%, list as "Supported (reduced perf)" with a note. <70% fails listing.

ajay: Works. We'll also require no functional mismatches on a short smoke eval (100 prompts, exact-match & logprob check). If any mismatch, mark as failing.

maria: Perfect. Who owns the telemetry schema and who vets kernel patches with partner?

tyler: I'll own telemetry schema and partner wrapper. Will hand them a small translator script that converts PDU CSV + runtime tel into our canonical fields. Plan to open PR with schema + example CSV parser.

ajay: I'll own kernel patch checklist and the microbench harness. I'll produce a 1-page patch matrix showing expected gains and risk level (low/med/high) for each change.

maria: Great. Deliverables: 1) telemetry schema + parser PR 2) patch matrix + microbench results 3) one-page marketplace blurb + recommended SKU. Draft due Tue EOD.

tyler: Draft telemetry CLI for partner (example):
```
# collect run
./rwd-collect --model redwood-7b-v2 --seq 256 --batch 64 --quant fp16 --pdu_csv /tmp/pdu.csv --out /tmp/run.json --sample-ms 250
```
I'll include a shim to align timestamps (pdu -> runtime) and compute tokens/sec/W.

ajay: For kernel tuning I'm proposing three experimental knobs: 1) warp-level matmul reorder 2) dynamic batch sharding 3) async-store for KV hot lanes. Each will include a regression harness and a perf threshold to accept.

maria: Ops-bot, can you schedule a partner lab slot on lab-7 for 2h tomorrow and post the run id here?

ops-bot: Booked partner-lab-7 for 2026-04-02 10:00 UTC. Run slot id: rp-5210012. Please tag run in PRs.

tyler: Quick note: partner firmware only exposes IPMI with 1s resolution. We'll still collect PDU but will fallback to IPMI if PDU unavailable and annotate results accordingly.

ajay: Documenting that in the telemetry schema: field power_source = ["pdu","ipmi"], and field power_resolution_ms.

maria: One more thing: marketplace blurb must not exaggerate perf; use exact measured tokens/sec/W from the listed SKU and link to the raw tel file. We'll host raw artifacts on s3 with retention 180 days.

tyler: Uploaded a sample run to s3: s3://partners-bench/5210011111/sample-run.json. Also opened PR: https://git.redwood/partners/telemetry/pulls/22

ajay: Patch matrix PR incoming in ~3hrs. I'll add expected delta numbers and a recommended conservative default for marketplace.

maria: Thanks all. We'll review final artifacts Wed 11am PT and freeze the listing. :rocket:
